items.answer: (1) S-waves travel only through solids. (2) S-waves do not pass through the outer core, so it must be liquid.

(b) Why are the northern plains densely populated? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) The Himalayas give water to rivers and block cold winds. (2) The plains are the granaries of India. (3) The plateau is rich in minerals and forests. (4) Coasts and islands give ports, fishing and tourism. (b) (1) Fertile alluvial soil and plenty of water. (2) Level land makes farming, roads and towns easy to build.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) The Himalayas give water to rivers and block cold winds. (2) The plains are the granaries of India. (3) The plateau is rich in minerals and forests. (4) Coasts and islands give ports, fishing and tourism. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Fertile alluvial soil and plenty of water. (2) Level land makes farming, roads and towns easy to build.

items.stem:
(a) What evidence supports the idea that the continents were once joined? (3 marks)
(b) Why are most volcanoes found along plate boundaries? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Coastlines of South America and Africa fit like a jigsaw. (2) Same fossils found on continents now far apart. (3) Similar rocks and mountain belts across oceans. (4) Glacial deposits in now-tropical regions. (b) (1) Plates move apart or one sinks below another. (2) Magma rises easily through the weak zones.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Coastlines of South America and Africa fit like a jigsaw. (2) Same fossils found on continents now far apart. (3) Similar rocks and mountain belts across oceans. (4) Glacial deposits in now-tropical regions. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Plates move apart or one sinks below another. (2) Magma rises easily through the weak zones.

items.stem:
(a) Match each agent with two landforms it creates: river, wind, glacier, sea waves. (3 marks)
(b) Why are deltas very fertile? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) River: meanders, deltas. (2) Wind: sand dunes, mushroom rocks. (3) Glacier: U-shaped valleys, moraines. (4) Sea waves: sea caves, stacks. (b) (1) Rivers deposit fine silt rich in nutrients. (2) There is plenty of water for farming.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) River: meanders, deltas. (2) Wind: sand dunes, mushroom rocks. (3) Glacier: U-shaped valleys, moraines. (4) Sea waves: sea caves, stacks. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Rivers deposit fine silt rich in nutrients. (2) There is plenty of water for farming.

items.stem:
(a) Suggest three measures that can reduce loss of life in earthquake-prone areas such as Uttarakhand or Gujarat. (3 marks)
(b) Why do earthquakes occur frequently in the Himalayan region? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Earthquake-resistant buildings. (2) Drills and awareness in schools. (3) Early warning and emergency services. (4) Avoid building on steep, unstable slopes. (b) (1) The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate. (2) Stress builds up in rocks and is released suddenly.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Earthquake-resistant buildings. (2) Drills and awareness in schools. (3) Early warning and emergency services. (4) Avoid building on steep, unstable slopes. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate. (2) Stress builds up in rocks and is released suddenly.

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Weathering
2. Duns
3. Lithosphere
4. Mantle
Column B:
(p) The thick layer below the crust, extending to a depth of about 2,900 km
(q) The breaking down of rocks in place by heat, water, frost, chemicals or living things
(r) The rigid outer layer formed by the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle
(s) Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks, such as Dehradun
items.markingKey: (a) Weathering – the breaking down of rocks in place by heat, water, frost, chemicals or living things; Duns – longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks, such as Dehradun; Lithosphere – the rigid outer layer formed by the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle; Mantle – the thick layer below the crust, extending to a depth of about 2,900 km.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'meander'?
items.answer: A large loop in a river as it flows over a gentle slope
items.markingKey: (a) 'Meander' means a large loop in a river as it flows over a gentle slope; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: A large loop in a river as it flows over a gentle slope
The newer, fertile alluvium of the floodplains, renewed every year
Alfred Wegener's idea that the continents were once joined and have drifted apart
The innermost layer of the Earth, made mainly of nickel and iron

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: The Peninsular plateau was once part of the ancient landmass called Angara.
items.answer: False. The Peninsular plateau was once part of the ancient landmass called Gondwana.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: 'Gondwana' in place of 'Angara' (½ mark). The Peninsular plateau was once part of the ancient landmass called Gondwana.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The crust is the thickest layer of the Earth.
Reason (R): The core is made mainly of nickel and iron.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false – the crust is the thinnest layer; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Compare the eastern and western coastal plains. (3 marks)
(b) How are the Himalayas different from the Peninsular plateau in origin? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Western plain is narrow; eastern plain is broad. (2) Eastern rivers form deltas; western rivers form estuaries. (3) West: Konkan, Kannad, Malabar; east: Northern Circar, Coromandel. (b) (1) The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed from the Tethys sediments. (2) The plateau is an old, stable block that was part of Gondwana land.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Western plain is narrow; eastern plain is broad. (2) Eastern rivers form deltas; western rivers form estuaries. (3) West: Konkan, Kannad, Malabar; east: Northern Circar, Coromandel. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) The Himalayas are young fold mountains formed from the Tethys sediments. (2) The plateau is an old, stable block that was part of Gondwana land.

items.stem: Name any two fold mountain ranges.
items.answer: Any two of: Himalayas, Alps, Andes, Rockies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any two correct: Himalayas, Alps, Andes, Rockies.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 9 student on "Plate tectonics" and answer the questions that follow.
"The theory of continental drift was proposed by (A) ______ in 1912. The instrument that records earthquake waves is a (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why do earthquakes occur frequently in the Himalayan region? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Alfred Wegener (ii) seismograph (iii) (1) The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate. (2) Stress builds up in rocks and is released suddenly.
items.markingKey: (i) Alfred Wegener – 1 mark. (ii) seismograph – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) The Indian plate is still pushing into the Eurasian plate. (2) Stress builds up in rocks and is released suddenly.

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: A glacier carves a ______-shaped valley.
items.answer: U
items.markingKey: (b) A glacier carves a U-shaped valley.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in chronological order (earliest first):
I. Bhuj earthquake in Gujarat
II. Indian Ocean tsunami
III. Wegener proposes continental drift
IV. Latur earthquake in Maharashtra
items.answer: III, IV, I, II
items.markingKey: (c) Wegener proposes continental drift (1912); Latur earthquake in Maharashtra (1993); Bhuj earthquake in Gujarat (2001); Indian Ocean tsunami (2004).

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'bhangar'?
items.answer: The older alluvium of the northern plains, lying above the floodplains
items.markingKey: (b) 'Bhangar' means the older alluvium of the northern plains, lying above the floodplains; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: The belt of volcanoes and earthquakes around the edge of the Pacific Ocean
The older alluvium of the northern plains, lying above the floodplains
Waves of energy produced by earthquakes that help scientists study the Earth's interior
The outermost and lowest range of the Himalayas

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a landform made by sea waves?
items.answer: Barchan
items.markingKey: (c) Barchan is not a landform made by sea waves; Sea cave, Sea arch, Sea cliff are landforms made by sea waves.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): S-waves cannot pass through liquids.
Reason (R): The continental crust is made mainly of silica and alumina and is called magma.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The continental crust is made mainly of silica and alumina and is called sial.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Define the term 'fold mountains'.
items.answer: Mountains formed when layers of rock are squeezed and folded by colliding plates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: mountains formed when layers of rock are squeezed and folded by colliding plates.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 9 student on "Major physiographic divisions of India and how they were formed" and answer the questions that follow.
"The western coastal plain between Goa and Mangaluru is called the (A) ______ coast. The highest peak of the Peninsular plateau is (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why are the northern plains densely populated? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Kannad (ii) Anai Mudi (iii) (1) Fertile alluvial soil and plenty of water. (2) Level land makes farming, roads and towns easy to build.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: India's only active volcano is on Barren Island.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. India's only active volcano is on Barren Island.
